about.title: About NewsIQ
about.subtitle: The signal behind the headlines.
about.lead: NewsIQ is a multilingual global news platform focused on important world events and their potential impact on financial markets. We turn complex, fast-moving stories into clear, concise intelligence — with context for the world and impact for the markets.
about.missionText: Help readers, professionals and curious citizens understand the news that actually moves the world — not the loudest stories, but the most consequential ones — in their own language, in seconds, with honest sourcing.
about.howItWorksText: Our editorial team curates stories from a growing list of verified sources in 15 languages. Each story is reviewed, classified and, when relevant, paired with a structured market-impact analysis. We never auto-publish unverified content and we never present AI analysis as fact.

principles.sourcing: Source attribution is non-negotiable. Every story names where it came from, with a credibility score.
principles.languages: Multilingual by design. We publish in 15 locales and never assume English is the reader's language.
principles.ai: AI is an assistant, never the author. AI-generated analysis is clearly labelled and never replaces the source.
principles.markets: Market impact is described, never prescribed. We never say buy, sell, or hold.
principles.corrections: We publish corrections visibly and stand behind what we ship.

about.team: NewsIQ is built by a small team of journalists, engineers and AI researchers.

contact.title: Contact
contact.subtitle: Get in touch with the NewsIQ team.
contact.generalText: For press, partnerships and general questions, reach out and we will route you to the right person.
contact.pressText: Journalists can request comment, interviews, or data from our editorial team.
contact.responseTime: We typically respond within two business days.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.subtitle: These terms govern your use of newsiq.top.
terms.intro: By accessing or using NewsIQ, you agree to be bound by these Terms of Service. If you do not agree, please do not use the service.

service.title: 1. The service
service.body: NewsIQ is a multilingual news and market-intelligence platform. We provide short news articles, source attribution, structured market-impact analysis (where available) and editorial tools for authenticated users. Some features require an account; paid features require an active subscription.

content.title: 2. Content & intellectual property
content.body: All editorial content on NewsIQ is provided for personal, non-commercial use. Source articles remain the property of their original publishers. We do not republish full copyrighted articles — we summarize, attribute and link. Quoting brief excerpts is permitted with attribution.

ai.title: 3. AI analysis disclaimer
ai.body: Market-impact analysis on NewsIQ is generated by an AI assistant and reviewed by our editorial team. It is informational, not financial advice. It does not constitute a buy, sell, or hold recommendation. Always do your own research and consult a licensed professional before making investment decisions.

account.title: 4. Your account
account.body: You are responsible for your account credentials and for activity under your account. Free accounts grant access to short news and limited analysis; Pro accounts unlock the full analysis breakdown. Subscriptions are governed by our subscription terms and our payment processor.

conduct.title: 5. Acceptable use
conduct.body: Do not abuse the platform: no scraping at scale, no automated AI training on our content without permission, no attempts to bypass rate limits or paywalls, no harassment, no impersonation. We may suspend or terminate accounts that violate these rules.

changes.title: 6. Changes to the service
changes.body: We may add, remove, or change features at any time. We will notify you of material changes to paid features via email or in-app notice.

liability.title: 7. Limitation of liability
liability.body: NewsIQ is provided "as is" without warranty. To the maximum extent permitted by law, NewsIQ and its team are not liable for any indirect, incidental, or consequential damages arising from your use of the service.

governing.title: 8. Governing law
governing.body: These terms are governed by the laws of the jurisdiction in which NewsIQ operates, without regard to conflict-of-laws principles.

contact.title: 9. Contact
contact.body: Questions about these terms? Email legal@newsiq.top.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.subtitle: How NewsIQ handles your data.
privacy.intro: NewsIQ respects your privacy. This page describes what we collect, why, and how long we keep it.

collect.title: What we collect
collect.body: For anonymous visitors: standard server logs and aggregate analytics. For registered users: your email, display name, preferred language, and timezone. For Pro subscribers: billing is handled by a third-party payment processor; we never see your card number.

use.title: How we use it
use.body: To run the service: render localized content, remember your preferences, and process your account actions. We do not sell your data to third parties. We do not run third-party advertising trackers on newsiq.top.

cookies.title: Cookies
cookies.body: We use a small number of first-party cookies to keep you signed in, remember your language preference, and measure aggregate site performance. You can clear cookies in your browser at any time.

retention.title: Retention
retention.body: Account data is kept while your account is active. You can request deletion at any time from your profile page or by emailing privacy@newsiq.top. Anonymized analytics may be retained indefinitely.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.body: You can request a copy of your data, correct inaccurate data, or delete your account. Contact privacy@newsiq.top.

changes.title: Changes to this policy
changes.body: We will post material changes here with an updated date at the top of this page.

cookies.title: Cookies
cookies.subtitle: How NewsIQ uses cookies.
cookies.intro: NewsIQ uses a small number of first-party cookies. We do not run third-party advertising trackers.
cookies.whatBody: A session cookie to keep you signed in, a language preference cookie, and a theme preference cookie (light or dark mode).
cookies.thirdBody: If we ever embed a third-party player or analytics tool, we will surface a consent banner. Today, no third-party trackers load on the public site.
cookies.manageBody: You can clear cookies in your browser at any time. Doing so will sign you out and reset your language and theme preferences.

editorialPolicy.title: Editorial Policy
editorialPolicy.subtitle: How NewsIQ reports, reviews, and revises the news.
editorialPolicy.intro: NewsIQ is committed to accurate, sourced, multilingual news. This page explains our editorial standards and process.

sourcing.title: Sourcing
sourcing.body: Every published story names its source, with a reliability score. We publish in 15 languages and we never strip a story of its original attribution.

review.title: Review workflow
review.body: Stories move through four states: draft, pending review, approved, published. Ingestion pipelines only ever create pending-review posts. A human editor must explicitly approve a story before publication.

ai.title: AI in the newsroom
ai.body: We use AI to summarize, classify, and analyze market impact. We do not use AI to fabricate or invent facts. AI-generated analysis is clearly labelled and is reviewed by an editor before publication.

corrections.title: Corrections
corrections.body: When we get something wrong, we correct it visibly. The original story stays in the database for auditability; the public view reflects the correction.

feedback.title: Reporting concerns
feedback.body: Readers can report a story for review. Reports are reviewed by editors and acted on within 72 hours.

sourcePolicy.title: Source Policy
sourcePolicy.subtitle: What we publish, and what we do not.
sourcePolicy.intro: NewsIQ is only as good as its sources. This page describes how we choose, evaluate, and maintain the sources we rely on.

criteria.title: Inclusion criteria
criteria.body: We include news agencies, broadcasters, financial media, government and official sources, and a curated set of community sources. Each source has a public credibility score between 0 and 100. Sources below a minimum threshold are not promoted to the public feed.

verification.title: Verification
verification.body: Each source goes through a manual review before being marked as verified. Verification is revoked if the source repeatedly publishes demonstrably false or misleading content.

types.title: Source types
types.body: We distinguish news agencies, newspapers, broadcasters, financial media, government and official sources, blogs, social feeds, and eyewitness reports. Each type is treated differently in our pipeline and in the user interface.

removal.title: Removal
removal.body: Sources can be suspended or rejected by editors. Rejected sources are not syndicated. Suspended sources are kept for audit but do not appear in the public feed.

careers.title: Careers
careers.subtitle: Build the next era of global news with us.
careers.intro: NewsIQ is a small, remote-first team of journalists, engineers, and AI researchers. We hire for craft, judgment, and care.
careers.noRoles: We do not have any open roles right now. Follow us on social media to be notified when the next one opens.
careers.valuesText: Candor over polish. Source-first reporting. Multilingual by default. AI that augments the newsroom, not replaces it.
careers.howWeHireText: A short written exercise, a paid trial project for engineering roles, and two conversations. We respond to every applicant, every time.

advertising.title: Advertising
advertising.subtitle: Reach a global, multilingual, decision-maker audience.
advertising.intro: NewsIQ is read by investors, professionals, journalists, and curious citizens across 15 language markets. We do not run intrusive ads and we do not sell reader data.
advertising.formatsText: We support banner ads, sponsored article slots, and newsletter placements. All sponsored content is clearly labelled and is reviewed by our editorial team for factual accuracy.
guidelinesItems: No ads for products or services we would not use ourselves.
No ads that mislead the reader or impersonate editorial content.
No tracking pixels, retargeting, or third-party data brokers.
No ads targeted to readers under 18.
advertising.contact: For media kits, rates, and placements, email advertising@newsiq.top.

markets.title: Markets
markets.subtitle: How NewsIQ connects global events to financial markets.
markets.intro: Every important story on NewsIQ can be paired with a structured market-impact analysis. The analysis describes likely effects on relevant markets, without telling you what to buy, sell, or hold.

assetClasses.commodities: Commodities (Gold, Oil, Silver, Natural Gas, Copper, Agricultural)
assetClasses.forex: Forex (USD, EUR, JPY, GBP and more)
assetClasses.equities: Equities and indices (S&P 500, Nasdaq, Dow Jones, FTSE, DAX, Nikkei)

markets.howBody: A news story is classified and deconstructed by our editorial team. Our AI assistant then proposes a directional analysis: affected markets, direction, strength, time horizon, confidence, and key risks. Every analysis is reviewed by an editor before it goes live.
markets.disclaimerBody: Market-impact analysis on NewsIQ is AI-generated and editorially reviewed. It is informational, not financial advice. We never say buy, sell, or hold. Markets are uncertain and past performance does not guarantee future results. Always do your own research and consult a licensed professional.
markets.ctaBody: Open any story tagged as market-relevant to read the full structured breakdown.

faqs.q: What is the difference between Free and Pro?
faqs.a: Free shows you the news and a short AI preview. Pro unlocks the full structured breakdown: which markets, in which direction, with what strength and time horizon, plus the key risks and opportunities.
